TN-2025-HB1817.aiSummary: The law changes rules for commercial drivers who cannot read and speak English well enough to handle traffic signs, talk with the public, and fill out required reports. If an officer finds this during a safety check, the driver can be put out of service, the truck cannot keep going until a qualified substitute driver arrives, and the driver’s commercial license can be suspended until the driver passes a state English test. The employer is responsible for fines or fees tied to the suspension or getting the license back, and a violation is a Class C misdemeanor with a $500 fine for the employer. Parts of the law took effect when it became law, and the rest takes effect January 1, 2027.

TN-2025-SB1622.aiSummary: This law requires the Department of Children’s Services commissioner to create a statewide quality assurance program that uses monitoring, review, and feedback to track how services are working for children and families. The program must include county-level review groups, a state office and committee, and a public website grade for each county that is updated at least every six months. The commissioner must also send quarterly progress reports starting with the fiscal quarter ending September 30, 2026, and the law takes effect July 1, 2026.
